outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Controlling Generative Models
outline.description: The advent of large-scale text-to-image diffusion models represents a watershed moment in the history of computer graphics and artificial intelligence. These systems, such as Stable Diffusion, Imagen, and Glide, have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in synthesizing highly photorealistic images directly from textual descriptions. By leveraging massive datasets of paired text and image data alongside advanced architecture designs like Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) or Vector Quantized GANs to operate in compressed latent spaces, these models have moved beyond simple pattern recognition to genuine creative synthesis. outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Understanding Hyperspherical Energy as a Stability Metric
outline.description: When attempting to adapt massive text-to-image diffusion models like Stable Diffusion for specific downstream tasks, researchers face a fundamental dilemma: how to teach the model something new without unlearning what it already knows about the world. Traditional fine-tuning strategies rely on heuristic assumptions, often assuming that keeping the total squared difference between old and new weights small ensures stability. However, as highlighted in recent literature, this view misses a critical nuance inherent to how neural networks encode meaning. Central to the proposed Orthogonal Fine-tuning (OFT) methodology is a deeper, more robust mathematical concept known as **Hyperspherical Energy** (HE).
